vulnerable_statements.reason: pg->ept is used with no lock and no NULL check. When the rpmsg device is removed (or not probed yet), the remove path sets pg->ept to NULL. A client such as ucsi or battmgr can still call pmic_glink_send at that point, so a NULL or stale endpoint is passed to rpmsg_send and dereferenced. This is a NULL pointer dereference or use-after-free race.

suggested_fix: Take the pmic_glink state mutex (pg->state_lock) around the send. While holding it, check whether pg->ept is NULL and return an error such as -ECONNRESET if it is; otherwise call rpmsg_send. The rpmsg probe and remove paths must assign and clear pg->ept under the same lock, so the endpoint cannot disappear while a send is in progress.
